intent: Four original surface atlases; unchanged accepted folded-paper geometry

prompts.border:
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: original opaque base-color texture atlas for a realistic folded-paper game pickup, not a photograph of a prop.
Canvas: portrait 3:4 aspect ratio, ideally 1536 x 2048 pixels. Two equally sized landscape 3:2 paper faces stacked vertically. The TOP HALF is the printed/written front. The BOTTOM HALF is the blank reverse. Both halves fill the entire canvas edge-to-edge with paper; no photographed page boundary, no background, no gap or divider. Keep the center horizontal boundary invisible except for the front ending. All front marks must lie within its own half, with generous 9% side margins and 10% top/bottom margins measured within that half.
Material: photorealistic modestly handled matte paper stock with fine fibers and subtle localized grime, low-contrast small wrinkles, no heavily browned antique parchment. Flat neutral scan-like diffuse illumination. No highlights, no cast shadows, no strong fold stripe, no fake depth shading, no hard dark vignette; actual folds and silhouette come from geometry.
The full readable narrative stays in the game reader. This surface contains ONLY the exact short canonical excerpts specified below, not the full story. Absolutely no additional words, names, dates, stamps, numbers, seals, logos or pseudo-writing. No signatures unless explicitly specified. Bottom half remains blank paper with only subtle fibers and handling wear; NO readable or mirrored ghost writing.
Opaque image, no transparency or border, no props, no hands, no watermarks.
Front design: restrained utilitarian border-post shift record on neutral gray-cream office stock. Thin faded charcoal printed header and one fine horizontal rule. A short, slightly uneven blue-black ballpoint entry underneath; utilitarian handwritten text, not ornate calligraphy. Leave useful blank space. Exact text, in this order, each on its own line:
"BORDER POST 14"
"NIGHT SHIFT"
"02:10 — Eastern fence lights failed."
"Count batteries, not rumors."
"Sgt. A. Koivu"
Small header, not oversized poster typography. This is an ordinary used document, with no red emergency motif.
